svg.title: Probes reaching a board in a bed-of-nails fixture
svg.desc: Drawn to scale, side view. A 1.6 mm board carries its parts on top: an 0603 resistor, a radial capacitor 8 mm in diameter and 11.5 mm tall, and a connector 8 mm tall. On the left, all the test points are on the bottom of the board, the side with no parts, and spring-loaded probes rise from one plate of probes 10 mm thick, each in a replaceable receptacle; every probe is the same short length. On the right, the same board with one test point on top, 1 mm from the tall capacitor: a probe from a top plate needs a cut-out round the tall parts and a probe longer than the capacitor, squeezed into a 1 mm gap. It's marked to avoid.

g.text: Test point on the bottom, the side with no parts
Spring probe in a replaceable receptacle
One plate of probes, about 10 mm FR4
Production grade; acrylic or MDF for development
Probe longer than the part beside it
In a 1 mm gap; easily bent or knocked
Cut-out in the top plate to clear tall parts
Drawn to scale (probe tips simplified). Dimensions in mm.
A flying-probe tester can reach both sides, but one side is still quicker.
The left half is how a board should be laid out for a fixture; it can be flying-probed too.
